stories.title: Photos: Nepal begins burying flood victims in mass graves
stories.summary: The Hindu rituals of death, cremation, prayer and final farewell have been overwhelmed by the scale of the disaster. Nepal has begun burying the victims of the devastating flood that hit the mountainous country last week in mass graves after taking DNA samples. Nepal has begun burying victims of last week’s devastating flood in mass graves after taking DNA samples. Nepalese authorities said on Tuesday that 1,003 bodies had been recovered, with 3,916 people still listed as missing, following the massive surge of freezing water, rocks and debris that tore down Himalayan valleys on August 26. The deadly wave was triggered by a high-altitude glacial collapse, and then carved a path of destruction through the country. At a mass burial ground in Chitwan district, the Hindu rituals of death, cremation, prayer and final farewell have been overwhelmed by the scale of the disaster, as authorities bury unidentified bodies after DNA sampling because there are too many to store or identify individually. Police using a drone to search for survivors said on Tuesday they had found 24 bodies in a single house in Nuwakot district. At least 17 bodies have been recovered from rivers far downstream in India. Prime Minister Balendra Shah has described the catastrophe as “unimaginable and heartbreaking”.

stories.title: Bank of America vice president identified as victim in Times Square attack
stories.summary: Erin Piacenti identified as one of two victims in day-light stabbing at iconic New York City thoroughfare. Erin Piacenti died from her wounds following the afternoon attack in the iconic New York City thoroughfare the day earlier, according to Reuters news agency. Bloomberg News first reported Piacenti’s identity. Authorities had previously said a female attacker had stabbed a 32-year-old woman and a 68-year-old man on West 42nd Street and Seventh Avenue around 4:30 pm (20:30 GMT) on Monday. Police fatally shot the suspect at the scene. The man was hospitalised in stable condition. “We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague,” Bank of America said in a statement to Reuters. “She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. Our hearts go out to her family and all of her loved ones.” New York Police Department Commissioner Jessica Tisch said earlier the attack appeared random and unprovoked. She said that responding officers had opened fire after attempting to taser the attacker, but had failed to stop her from advancing towards them with knives. The attack comes weeks after Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty to federal charges connected to the December 2024 fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.

stories.title: Russia sanctions bill 'hanging by a thread' in US Congress — media
stories.summary: House Democrats fear that "the bill as written would give President Donald Trump even more tariff-related authorities that he could abuse"
article_sentences: WASHINGTON, September 1.
A bill to toughen sanctions against Russia is currently "hanging by a thread" in the US Congress, according to Punchbowl News.

According to the news portal, House Democrats fear that "the bill as written would give President Donald Trump even more tariff-related authorities that he could abuse." "Key House Democrats are doubling down on their opposition to the Senate-passed bill, insisting that Trump already has ample existing authority to impose the types of sanctions on Moscow that are outlined in the legislation," it said.
"The Russia sanctions bill is hanging on a thread," the portal stated.
Leader of the Democratic minority in the House of Representatives Hakeem Jeffries (New York) said earlier that some of the House Democrats oppose the bill on tougher anti-Russian sanctions.
The Russian sanctions bill was initiated by a group of US lawmakers in the House of Representatives in August.
A similar bill was approved by the US Senate on August 7.
As media outlets previously reported, a number of lawmakers had expressed concerns over provisions that could significantly expand US President Donald Trump's authority to impose import tariffs.
The bill envisages restrictions against senior Russian political and military officials and state-owned companies, as well as secondary sanctions against Russia's trading partners.
Under the bill, the United States could impose 100% tariffs on countries that are major buyers of Russian oil and gas.
The bill also toughens sanctions against Iran.

stories.title: Bessent says his goal to force Iran to strike deal with US through sanctions
stories.summary: The US treasury secretary said that Washington is going "to economically asphyxiate" Tehran
article_sentences: WASHINGTON, September 1.
The US administration wants to use sanctions to force Tehran to enter into an agreement with Washington, said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Responding to journalists’ questions during the meeting of finance ministers and central bank governors of the Group of Twenty (G20) countries in Asheville (North Carolina), he said that the United States is going "to economically asphyxiate this regime."
"And as [US] President [Donald] Trump said, the reason the memorandum of understanding did not work - they were not ready for a deal.
My job is to make sure that they want to have a deal, and they will want to have one," the minister said.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28.
In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding providing for an immediate cessation of hostilities on all fronts, including in Lebanon.
However, on the night of July 8, the United States resumed large·scale strikes against Iran, accusing it of violating the agreements on the Strait of Hormuz.
On August 24, Bessent said that Washington was tightening unilateral sanctions against Iran sharply, aiming to sever Tehran’s sources of income.

stories.title: Boris Vujčić: Household expectations and monetary policy: The importance of high-quality surveys and evidence-based research
article_sentences: Thank you, Michael, and thank you to ESMT for the invitation.

It is a pleasure to be here for this inauguration and to speak about a topic to which Michael has made an outstanding contribution: how households form expectations and why those expectations matter for monetary policy.
Monetary policy is, by its nature, forward-looking.
We track inflation, wages, consumption, credit and financial conditions.

But none of these data fully tell us what households believe and how these beliefs feed into their economic and financial decisions, how uncertain they are, or why similar shocks produce different responses across population sub-groups and countries.
The insights from expectations surveys matter, because expectations about the future shape decisions and behaviour today.
Expectations about inflation, income, employment, interest rates and house prices affect spending, saving, investment, borrowing and wage demands.
They therefore play a key role in shaping the transmission mechanism of monetary policy.
This became much more feasible as the internet and mobile technologies became more widely used.
Online survey data collection, better questionnaire design and more effective sampling methods now allow high-quality, population-representative evidence to be collected in a very timely manner.

The ECB’s Consumer Expectations Survey is a case in point, as is the recent work by the Bank for International Settlements.[2] This research programme has improved our understanding of expectations formation and its role in shaping aggregate economic outcomes.
Alexander von Humboldt would no doubt have approved of this enhanced approach to measuring expectations because it follows his maxim about observing carefully before generalising.
